units: <cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 11">Ex. R. s. 11</cite> [read:] <he>כאדם שאומר לחבירו לא יטול פלוני ק׳ זו … עליו</he> like a man saying to his neighbor, that man will not undergo that sentence, for such and such stands by him as his patron.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 30">Ex. R. s. 30</cite> [read:] <he>נתן ק׳ לקומיס</he> he passed sentence on the Comes; <he>נתן ק׳ לאברהם</he> he sentenced Abraham (thy seed shall be strangers &c., <cite ref="Genesis 15:13">Gen. XV, 13</cite>).

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 18">Lev. R. s. 18</cite>, end <he>בו״ד גובה ק׳ וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="S00772"><he>קטירקי</he></cite>) a human being (king) collects a fine, and so does the Lord (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:19">Deut. XXII, 19</cite>); <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7:3">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>יש לו קטריקס</he> (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3:15">Deut. R. s. 3</cite> <he>בניך חוטאין ואתה נותן עלי ק׳</he> thy children sinned, and me thou punishest? <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 3">Ib.</cite> <he>לתת עליך ק׳ אתה וכ׳</he> (I want) to fine thee; thou hast broken them (the tablets) and thou must replace them.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 5:12:1">Koh. R. to V, 12</cite> <he>היא ק׳ דידיה … ק׳ דמלכות וכ׳</he> it (his wealth) is his punishment; when a verdict from the government comes out against him, he will give whatever he has (to be released).
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 10:1">Pesik. R. s. 10</cite> <he>מהו ק׳ שלו</he> what is the fine he has to pay?; a. e.
